/-!
# Conjecture 5.56

by J. Wiegold

a) Let $p$ be a prime greater than $3$. Is it true that every finite group of
exponent $p$ can be embedded in the commutator subgroup of a finite group of
exponent $p$?

Only part a) of Problem 5.56 remains in the current edition of the notebook.

The restriction $p > 3$ excludes the primes for which the answer is negative:
every group of exponent $2$ is abelian, so its commutator subgroup is trivial,
and the commutator subgroup of every group of exponent $3$ is abelian.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.56».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → 3 < p →
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], Monoid.exponent G = p →
        ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H), Monoid.exponent H = p ∧
          ∃ f : G →* commutator H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $p$ be a prime greater than $3$. Is it true that every finite group $G$ of
exponent $p$ can be embedded in the commutator subgroup of a finite group of
exponent $p$? That is, is there a finite group $H$ of exponent $p$ and an
injective homomorphism $G \to [H, H]$?

"Exponent $p$" is stated as `Monoid.exponent G = p`. Since $p$ is prime, this is
equivalent to $G$ being non-trivial with $x^p = 1$ for all $x \in G$; the
trivial group is excluded, which is harmless since it embeds in any group.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (the only remaining lettered part, unstarred so still open): implicitly quantified over all primes p > 3 and all finite groups G of exponent p, asking for a finite group H of exponent p and an injective homomorphism G → commutator H (i.e. G isomorphic to a subgroup of the derived subgroup H'); 'exponent p' should be read as x^p = 1 for all x (or Monoid.exponent = p, the trivial group being a harmless edge case), and the restriction p > 3 is essential since exponent-2 groups are abelian and exponent-3 groups have too small derived subgroups.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematics faithfully (∀ prime p > 3, ∀ finite G of exponent p, ∃ finite H of exponent p with an injective hom G →* commutator H). c06 chosen as base: repo-conventional theorem name kourovka.«5.56».parts.a inside namespace Kourovka.«5.56» (c03/c08 deviate with bare parts.a), literal `Monoid.exponent G = p` reading (verified in Lean to be equivalent, for finite G and prime p, to nontrivial ∧ ∀ x, x^p = 1, so it differs from c01/c02/c07's reading only on the harmless trivial group), direct injective hom into `commutator H` (equivalent to c01/c04's range ≤ commutator), and complete module/theorem docstrings. I edited the module docstring's explanation of the p > 3 restriction (c06's phrasing 'a non-abelian group of exponent p can never be embedded' was vacuous for p = 2) to the accurate version from c05 (exponent-2 groups are abelian so their commutator subgroup is trivial; commutator subgroup of an exponent-3 group is abelian), and added c05's note that only part a) remains in the notebook.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.56

by J. Wiegold

a) Let $p$ be a prime greater than $3$. Is it true that every finite group of
exponent $p$ can be embedded in the commutator subgroup of a finite group of
exponent $p$?

Only part a) of Problem 5.56 remains in the current edition of the notebook.

The restriction $p > 3$ excludes the primes for which the answer is negative:
every group of exponent $2$ is abelian, so its commutator subgroup is trivial,
and the commutator subgroup of every group of exponent $3$ is abelian.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.56»

/--
Let $p$ be a prime greater than $3$. Is it true that every finite group $G$ of
exponent $p$ can be embedded in the commutator subgroup of a finite group of
exponent $p$? That is, is there a finite group $H$ of exponent $p$ and an
injective homomorphism $G \to [H, H]$?

"Exponent $p$" is stated as `Monoid.exponent G = p`. Since $p$ is prime, this is
equivalent to $G$ being non-trivial with $x^p = 1$ for all $x \in G$; the
trivial group is excluded, which is harmless since it embeds in any group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.56».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → 3 < p →
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], Monoid.exponent G = p →
        ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H), Monoid.exponent H = p ∧
          ∃ f : G →* commutator H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.56»

items: 'Group of exponent p' is formalized as `Monoid.exponent G = p` (Mathlib's exact exponent) for both G and H. Since p is prime this is equivalent to 'G is non-trivial and x^p = 1 for all x'. The alternative reading `∀ x, x ^ p = 1` differs only by admitting the trivial group, which embeds in any group, so the two readings yield equivalent problems; the choice is documented in the theorem docstring.

Embedding 'in the commutator subgroup of H' is stated as `∃ f : G →* commutator H, Function.Injective f`, where `commutator H = ⁅(⊤ : Subgroup H), ⊤⁆` is Mathlib's derived subgroup, coerced to a type.

Both G and H are taken in `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76); H is existentially quantified after G, so it may depend on G, matching 'a finite group of exponent p'.
Finiteness is expressed with `Finite` (instance binder for G, existential binder `(_ : Finite H)` for H) rather than `Fintype`, since no computation on cardinality is needed.

The module docstring explains the domain restriction p > 3: exponent-2 groups are abelian and the derived subgroup of any exponent-3 group is abelian (exponent-3 groups are nilpotent of class ≤ 3, so [G',G'] ≤ γ₄(G) = 1), so non-abelian groups of exponent ≤ 3 can never embed in such a commutator subgroup.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted anything and no decomposition objections were raised. Two acceptable readings of 'exponent p' exist (Monoid.exponent G = p vs ∀ x, x^p = 1); they differ only for the trivial group (which embeds in any group), so the truth value of the question is identical under both — this is documented in the theorem docstring. The question is read as a single yes/no question quantified over all primes p > 3 (per repo convention 'put all quantifiers after answer(sorry)'); a per-p answer is not separately expressible with answer(sorry) and the notebook treats it as one question. Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), which loses nothing for finite groups and matches the existing Kourovka files. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
